themes: Round 4 improves situation diversity, but several replacements change the wrapper more than the decision.
FUN answers still lean heavily on short action fragments followed by a punchline. HEART often expands those fragments without finding a distinct, calmer voice.
The repeated four-answer ladder remains visible: wholehearted yes, reluctant yes, qualified refusal, firm refusal.
Dogs, cats, cabins and group chats still exceed the two-card prop limit.
Some cards measure attachment, publicity, advice-taking or shared ownership instead of their stated sub-question.
Several weaker answers manufacture privacy or autonomy symbolically without actually preserving either.
Intentional feeling follow-ups are legitimate continuations, not separate scenario inventions. Their repeated props still contribute to prop counts.
No em dashes or prohibited genie, lamp, wish-granting or wizard tropes found in the after-bank.

repeats.what: A long-silent friendship disables a magical household object; acceptance and renewed contact oppose reproach and punitive exclusion. The plant and chair are different props around the same situation.

Magical visible achievement displays make personal progress comparable to other people's progress: the life-ranking billboard, relationship percentages and work-star door. The billboard feeling follow-up is included in this over-limit cluster.

themes: Round 6 resolves the friendship-silence, jacket and spreadsheet clusters identified in round 5.

Too many answers use the same clipped sequence: accept or refuse, then a comic consequence. HEART often preserves that rhythm instead of becoming calm, complete prose.

Some revisions repair surface wording without repairing measurement: attendance is not group conformity, impatience is not checking progress, and handing something over in person is not having a conversation.
Real and receipts cards provide useful grounding, but repeated 'last time', 'think of' and 'tap every' openings flatten their individual voices.
The strongest spice exposes envy, resentment, concealed boundaries or competing loyalties. Several magical props supply novelty without creating a difficult choice.
No genie, lamp, wish-granting or wizard trope, and no em dash, found in the current card text.
Feeling follow-ups serve a different function from their preceding choices; their permitted two-card situation pairs are not redundant reframings.
